lines.plain: What is the physics of a bridge?

actions.text: A suspension bridge hangs its deck from cables. The cables are pulled tight (tension) and rest on the towers, which are squeezed (compression) and pass the weight into the ground. Turn the model and tap a part to see its job.

parts.name: Road deck
parts.explain: The road surface. Traffic sits on it, and it bends a little between hangers before passing the weight down to the girders.

parts.name: Stiffening girder
parts.explain: A deep steel box under the road. It stiffens the deck so it doesn't sag or twist between hangers: it works in bending.

parts.name: Left tower
parts.explain: The cables rest on its top, so the weight of the whole deck pushes straight down through it into the pier: compression.

parts.name: Left pier
parts.explain: The foundation block under the tower. It spreads the tower's push into the ground.

parts.name: Left anchorage
parts.explain: A huge block of concrete that holds the cable ends down. Its weight resists the cable's pull.

parts.name: Main cable
parts.explain: Hangs between the tower tops and is pulled tight by everything hanging from it, so it is in tension all along.

parts.name: Back stay
parts.explain: Carries the cable's pull from the tower top down to the anchorage, balancing the main span so the tower isn't pulled over.
